 Judgment
Dated this the 21st .day of November, 2025 Nitin Jamdar, C. J.

Heard Mr. V. Harish, the learned counsel for the Petitioner, Mr.B. Pramod, the learned Senior Panel Counsel for Respondent Nos.1 and 2, Ms. Chithra P George, the learned Standing Counsel for Respondent No.3 and Mr. P.G. Pramod, the learned Government Pleader for Respondent No.4.

2 . This petition is filed for directions to the statutory authorities particularly, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India to address the issue of microplastic contamination, which is alleged to be present in bottled drinking water.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In the petition the Petitioner has elaborated various aspects of the microplastics and the fact that microplastics in bottled drinking water is not regulated.
3. The learned counsel for the Petitioner accepts that what is required is the exercise of framing of appropriate regulation.
The learned counsel also submits that at the first instance, the Respondents be called upon to look into the representation of the Petitioner highlighting the need for framing of regulation.

sentences.text: 4. The Petitioner has already made a detailed representation in that regard, which is annexed as Ext.P13.
Let the Respondent No.3 look 2025:KER:89619 into the representation made by the Petitioner as regards its feasibility, correctness and other parameters.

It is for the Respondent No.3,
statutory authority to take necessary decisions in that regard.
5. With these observations, the writ petition is disposed of.
The response of Respondent No.3 to the representation of the Petitioner be communicated to the Petitioner.
Though we at at present not fixing any specific timeline as it is a policy matter, we expect the authority to look into the representation at the earliest.

Sd/-
